Please do not flame me for my opinions :(

Crayne addressed your comments. There's no flaming going on.

Allow me to further address your comments.

You display no evidence in your commentary that you've done anything more than skim the piece over, let alone thought about it for any length of time. You can't even be bothered to leave feedback with proper spelling or grammar. And then you say stuff like "feels like its just written so you can get words down," while having the temerity to act butthurt when Crayne offers a counterpoint.

I've been downvoted and criticized dozens of times on this site. It's never bothered me, because in those cases people have taken the time to read something that I've written, and offered me the benefit of their insight, which has helped me to improve as a writer. I welcome that kind of scrutiny.

You, on the other hand, don't even appear to have a proper grasp of basic English. Feel free to vote however you wish on my work or anything else on the site. But I sure as hell am not going to take any commentary from you seriously. I have no respect for amateurish, ill-informed criticism, wherever it appears. And that's the last I'm going to say on the matter.

item.content:encoded:
How are there a hundred ways to interpret that? It seemed fairly obvious. The man was a Church of the Broken God spy. He has been mostly replaced by mechanics on the inside, and finally decides to leave his human body behind, but keeps it intact so it can run errands for him.

As it moves, I can hear the the tiny little servos implanted throughout it, located at key joints and around the vital organs.

You can only get so much out of an artificial neural unit; fusing it to the spine didn't leave a lot of room to work with.

These show the body is mechanically supported. It's not just the skin, but most of the muscles and organs, which are not needed by his now mechanical body.

As for the girl praying, she's a member of a foundation task force sent to Venus with the rest of the colonists. She's praying because she's stressed and trying to get ready before landing. We can also see other task force members trying to relieve stress through various methods.

Overall, the message seemed pretty clear to me. Can't figure out where you got "bouncy blue ball" from, can't find it in the stories.

I do have once suggestion though. The article might be more clear if you had a link to the original SCP these people are sent to explore somewhere on the page, or the specific MTF series these articles belong to.
